newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks erase gains to end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks erase gains to end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks surrendered early gains and closed marginally lower on Wednesday as profit-taking emerged after the market digested news U.S. interest rates had been left unchanged, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index eased 0.68 of a point to close at 14,235.52 after hitting a record high of 14,398.55. Turnover was HK$16.15 billion versus Tuesday's HK$12.75 billion.

"Stocks rose earlier on the rates news but after taking a second thought people found this has been priced in," said Franco Tong, in institutional sales at New China Hong Kong. "The market has been overbought and should come down a bit."
Brokers said index futures-related selling was seen on HSBC Holdings and Hutchison in late trade.
HSBC was unchanged at HK$220.00 after erased a HK$2.00 gain earlier and Hutchison retreated from a high of HK$64.50 to close at HK$63.25, up HK$0.25.
"The market is heading for a correction and this is natural after the recent record-setting sessions," said Henry Lui, an analyst at Mansion House Research.
Property stocks were generally lower on profit-taking with Cheung Kong easing HK$0.50 to HK$78.50. Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$1.75 to close at HK$94.50.
Lui said the market focus shifted to red-chips as investors believed the upside on blue chips was limited.

Analysts said the fever surrounding the initial public offering of Beijing Enterprises shares also helped boosted red-chips. "Many investors turned to the listed red-chips because at least they are available in the market," one said.
The Beijing Enterprises share offer was expected to draw over a thousand times subscription.
China Merchant jumped HK$1.50, or 15.71 percent, to HK$11.05, Guangnan surged HK$0.45 to HK$11.35 and China Resources added HK$1.30 at HK$24.00.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index for H-shares soared 16.43 points, or 1.57 percent, to 1,065.69.
Guangdong Kelon rose HK$0.70 to HK$8.00 and Zhejiang Expressway added HK$0.22 at HK$2.85 but Qingling Motors fell HK$0.22 to HK$3.70.
Brokers said the overall sentiment on Hong Kong stocks remained bullish and a correction would be healthy for the market before the Hang Seng gets set for its next rally.
